beats.say: One programmer created the world's most famous game in just three weeks.
In the mid-1980s, Alexey Pajitnov was working at the Dorodnitsyn Computing Center in Moscow.
He developed Tetris for the Elektronika 60 before porting it to the IBM PC.
Floppy disk copies were distributed freely throughout Moscow before spreading across Eastern Europe.
Robert Stein saw the game in Hungary and sublicensed it to Mirrorsoft and Spectrum HoloByte.
Henk Rogers later negotiated with Elektronorgtechnica to secure the rights for Nintendo.
Nintendo released their version in 1989, turning a Soviet experiment into a global phenomenon.
Which version of Tetris was your first?

facts: Alexey Pajitnov created Tetris in the mid-1980s in about three weeks
Pajitnov worked at the Dorodnitsyn Computing Center of the Academy of Sciences
The game was initially programmed in Pascal for the Elektronika 60
The game was ported to the IBM PC using Turbo Pascal
Floppy disk copies spread from Moscow to Eastern Europe
Robert Stein saw Tetris in Hungary and secured a license
Stein sublicensed the game to Mirrorsoft and Spectrum HoloByte
Henk Rogers negotiated with Elektronorgtechnica for Nintendo
